c1.fil: Hello? Migo? Si Tita Cora 'to. Nakarating ka na ba sa bahay ni Lola?
c1.en: Hello? Migo? It's Tita Cora. Did you make it to Lola's house?

c1.fil: Pasensya ka na, anak, ha. Ikaw lang talaga ang puwedeng magbantay diyan habang nasa probinsya kami.
c1.en: I'm sorry, anak. You're the only one who can watch the house while we're in the province.

c1.fil: Hindi puwedeng walang tao diyan hangga't hindi pa tapos ang apatnapung araw ni Lola. Alam mo naman ang pamahiin.
c1.en: Someone has to be there until Lola's forty days are over. You know the old belief.

c1.fil: Noong bata pa ako, ayaw ni Lola na may natutulog nang bukas ang pinto. Gabi-gabi, siya mismo ang nagsasara ng lahat. Ang pinto, ang kurtina, pati ang aparador niya.
c1.en: When I was little, Lola never let anyone sleep with the door open. Every night she closed everything herself. The door, the curtain, even her aparador.

c1.fil: Ang aparador na 'yan, bigay raw ng dati niyang kumare sa San Lucio. Mula nang dumating 'yan, may naririnig na kaming kaluskos sa loob. Parang may gumagapang.
c1.en: That aparador was a gift from an old friend of hers in San Lucio. Ever since it came, we'd hear scratching inside. Like something crawling.

c1.fil: Noong huling linggo bago siya nawala, sabi niya may babaeng nakaputi raw na nakatayo sa pasilyo tuwing alas-tres. At may lumilipad daw sa may bintana.
c1.en: In her last week, she said a woman in white stood in the hallway every night at three. And that something flew past the window.

c1.fil: Akala namin, dahil lang sa gamot niya. Pero noong lamay, nakita ng Tito mo na bukas ang kurtina, at may mga kalmot sa rehas.
c1.en: We thought it was just her medicine. But during the wake, your Tito found the curtain open, and claw marks on the window bars.

c1.fil: Migo, makinig ka. Hindi ako nagbibiro.
c1.en: Migo, listen to me. I'm not joking.

c1.fil: Hindi sumasara nang kusa ang pinto ng kwartong 'yan. Kapag may narinig kang humihinga sa likod nito, isara mo, at huwag mong bibitawan hangga't hindi siya umaalis.
c1.en: That bedroom door never stays shut by itself. If you hear breathing behind it, close it, and don't let go until she leaves.

c1.fil: Kapag nakapasok siya, magtago ka sa ilalim ng kama. At habang nasa kwarto siya, huwag kang hihinga.
c1.en: If she gets in, hide under the bed. And as long as she's in the room, don't breathe.

c1.fil: Sumilip ka sa kurtina paminsan-minsan. Kapag nakita mo siyang papalapit, isara mo at hawakan hanggang lumipad siya palayo.
c1.en: Look behind the curtain every now and then. If you see her coming, close it and hold it until she flies away.

c1.fil: At kapag may kaluskos sa aparador, ilawan mo agad. Ayaw nila sa liwanag.
c1.en: And if something rustles in the aparador, shine a light on it right away. They hate the light.

c1.fil: Pagsapit ng alas-sais, tutunog ang kampana ng simbahan. Saka ka lang ligtas.
c1.en: At six, the church bell will ring. Only then are you safe.

c1.fil: Sige na, anak. Matulog ka na. Teka, sino 'yang kasama mo diyan? Bakit may naririnig akong humihinga sa tabi mo?
c1.en: Go on, anak. Get some sleep. Wait, who's there with you? Why do I hear someone breathing right next to you?

c1n1.fil: Migo, gising ka pa? Huwag mong kalimutan ang pinto.
c1n1.en: Migo, still awake? Don't forget the door.

c1n1.fil: Pakinggan mo muna. Kapag may humihinga na sa kabila, huwag mo nang ilawan. Isara mo na lang, at huwag kang bibitaw.
c1n1.en: Listen first. If something is already breathing on the other side, don't shine your light. Just close it, and don't let go.

c1n2.fil: Migo, kapag tumahimik ang mga kuliglig sa labas, silipin mo ang kurtina.
c1n2.en: Migo, when the crickets outside go quiet, check behind the curtain.

c1n2.fil: Kapag nakita mo siyang papalapit, isara mo at hawakan. Matagal bago siya sumuko, kaya huwag mong bibitawan.
c1n2.en: If you see her coming, close it and hold it. She takes a long time to give up, so don't let go.

c1n3.fil: Migo, may narinig ka bang gumagapang sa loob ng aparador?
c1n3.en: Migo, have you heard something crawling inside the aparador?

c1n3.fil: Ilawan mo. Paulit-ulit. Huwag mong hayaang bumukas nang tuluyan ang pinto niyan.
c1n3.en: Shine your light on it. Again and again. Don't let that door swing all the way open.

c1n4.fil: Gising silang lahat ngayong gabi. Ang pinto, ang kurtina, ang aparador.
c1n4.en: They're all awake tonight. The door, the curtain, the aparador.

c1n4.fil: Makinig ka lang. Sila mismo ang magsasabi sa'yo kung nasaan sila.
c1n4.en: Just listen. They'll tell you where they are.

c1n5.fil: Migo, papatayin daw ang kuryente sa barangay mamayang alas-kuwatro.
c1n5.en: Migo, they said the barangay will cut the power at four.

c1n5.fil: Tipirin mo ang flashlight. Kahit anong marinig mo, huwag kang lalabas ng kwarto.
c1n5.en: Save your flashlight. Whatever you hear, don't leave the room.

c1n5.fil: Migo? Bakit bukas ang ilaw diyan? Akala ko wala nang kuryente.
c1n5.en: Migo? Why is the light on over there? I thought the power was out.

c2n1.fil: Migo, si Tita Cora ulit. Nakaligtas ka sa kwarto ng Lola mo. Pero simula ngayong gabi, huwag ka nang babalik doon.
c2n1.en: Migo, it's Tita Cora again. You survived your Lola's room. But from tonight on, don't go back in there.

c2n1.fil: Dito ka na sa pasilyo. Mula diyan, abot mo ang sala, ang kusina, at ang kurtina sa likod na pinto.
c2n1.en: Stay in the hallway now. From there you can reach the living room, the kitchen and the curtain on the back door.

c2n1.fil: Kapag bumukas nang kusa ang TV sa sala at may umiiyak na sanggol, puntahan mo agad at patayin ang TV.
c2n1.en: If the TV in the living room turns on by itself and you hear a baby crying, go at once and switch it off.

c2n1.fil: Kapag tumawa na siya, huwag mong buksan ang ilaw. Magtago ka sa sopa at huwag kang gagalaw.
c2n1.en: If it starts laughing, don't turn on the light. Hide on the sofa and don't move.

c2n1.fil: At ang kurtina sa likod. Kapag tumahimik ang kuliglig, silipin mo. Kapag nasa salamin na siya, isara at hawakan.
c2n1.en: And the curtain at the back. When the crickets go quiet, look. If she's at the glass, close it and hold it.

c2n2.fil: Migo, may naririnig ka bang kalansing sa kusina? Parang kutsara at kutsilyong nagbabanggaan?
c2n2.en: Migo, do you hear clinking in the kitchen? Like spoons and knives knocking together?

c2n2.fil: Ang asin sa garapon, sa tabi ng kalan. Kapag papalapit na ang kalansing, ihagis mo ang asin.
c2n2.en: The salt in the jar, beside the stove. When the clinking comes close, throw the salt.

c2n2.fil: Kapag nasa loob na siya ng kusina, magtago ka sa paminggalan at huwag kang gagalaw kahit anong mangyari.
c2n2.en: If it's already inside the kitchen, hide in the cupboard and don't move, no matter what.

c2n3.fil: Gising na silang tatlo, Migo. Ang TV, ang kusina, ang kurtina.
c2n3.en: All three are awake now, Migo. The TV, the kitchen, the curtain.

c2n3.fil: Huwag kang tatakbo kung hindi kailangan. Naririnig nila ang yabag mo.
c2n3.en: Don't run unless you have to. They can hear your footsteps.

c2n4.fil: Migo, makinig ka. Ngayong gabi, may papatay ng kuryente mula sa may sala. Hindi brownout iyon.
c2n4.en: Migo, listen. Tonight someone will switch the power off from the living room side. It isn't a brownout.

c2n4.fil: Nasa kusina ang breaker. Tandaan mo ang pagkakasunod ng mga ilaw, saka mo ulitin. Isang beses lang niya ipapakita.
c2n4.en: The breaker is in the kitchen. Remember the order of the lights, then repeat it. It shows only once.

c2n5.fil: Huling gabi sa labas ng kwarto, Migo. Dalawang beses nilang papatayin ang kuryente.
c2n5.en: Last night outside the bedroom, Migo. They will cut the power twice.

c2n5.fil: Tipirin mo ang flashlight. Kapag nagkamali ka sa breaker, maririnig nila.
c2n5.en: Save your flashlight. If you get the breaker wrong, they will hear it.

c2n5.fil: Pagsikat ng araw, tapos na. Kaya mo 'to.
c2n5.en: When the sun comes up, it's over. You can do this.
